title: Bounded finite constant chain maps are locally algebraic
statement: Let C be a category with a precoverage J satisfying the site covering axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let R be a commutative ring. Let F and G be cochain complexes of R-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Suppose F is zero outside a bounded interval and each term of F is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Use the termwise constant-module functor [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor, lem-sfb-perfect-constant-local-chain-representative]. For any object U and chain map a between the restrictions of the constant F and G to C/U [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], there is a covering presieve S of U such that for every g : V → U in S there exists an algebraic chain map b : F → G whose constant realization restricted to V equals the further restriction of a, in each degree. No boundedness or finiteness of G, projectivity of F, terminal object of C, or derived-category instances are required.

source.place: Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map: the chain-map step after Tag 09BD, using Modules on Sites Tag 093S(3), lemma-morphism-locally-constant.

proof.text: For each source term, choose finitely many generators. Lift their images on a common covering using the finite-family constant-section lifting theorem (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.ConstantSheafSections, GrothendieckTopology.exists_mem_forall_exists_toSheafify_const_app_eq). On any object not covered by the empty sieve, GrothendieckTopology.toSheafify_const_app_injective makes the constant unit injective. Module sheafification supplies a linear unit. The range of the map on constant sections is contained in the range of that unit because it contains the generator images; the inverse linear equivalence onto the range constructs an algebraic linear map. Separatedness and local surjectivity of the unit prove equality of the induced module-sheaf morphisms throughout the slice. No slice-constant comparison is required.

There are only finitely many source degrees in the support interval. Intersect their covering sieves using GrothendieckTopology.iInf_mem. Induct on the generated Grothendieck topology to refine this sieve by a J-covering presieve: identities use the isomorphism axiom, pullbacks use the covering-family pullback axiom, and transitivity uses bind composition. On nonempty-covered members choose the component linear maps and set every other degree to zero; the zero-source API proves component equality outside the interval. Reflect all chain equations through injective constant units, using the given chain equations and functoriality of restriction. On empty-covered members use the zero chain map; separatedness makes every two restricted module morphisms equal. This yields the claimed algebraic chain map, including the support boundary cases.

theorem exists_bounded_constant_chain_map_local
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (J : Precoverage C) (hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings)
    (R : Type (max u v)) [CommRing R]
    (F G : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ)
    (hF : ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero (F.X q))
    [∀ q : ℤ, Module.Finite R (F.X q)] (U : C)
    (a : (moduleCochainRestriction
        ((constantSheaf J.toGrothendieck RingCat.{max u v}).obj (RingCat.of R)) U).obj
        ((constantModuleCochainFunctor J.toGrothendieck R).obj F) ⟶
      (moduleCochainRestriction
        ((constantSheaf J.toGrothendieck RingCat.{max u v}).obj (RingCat.of R)) U).obj
        ((constantModuleCochainFunctor J.toGrothendieck R).obj G)) :
    ∃ S : Presieve U, S ∈ J U ∧
      ∀ (V : C) (g : V ⟶ U), S g → ∃ b : F ⟶ G, ∀ q : ℤ,
        (SheafOfModules.overMap
          ((constantSheaf J.toGrothendieck RingCat.{max u v}).obj (RingCat.of R)) g).map
          (a.f q) =
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor
          ((constantSheaf J.toGrothendieck RingCat.{max u v}).obj (RingCat.of R)) V).map
          ((siteConstantModuleFunctorGeneral J.toGrothendieck R).map (b.f q))
